item.title: Psychological assessment delays sentencing in Longford arson case
item.description: A psychological assessment is to be carried out on a man responsible for an arson incident in Longford town. The fire caused several million euro worth of damage to businesses in Grafton Court in July 2024. Chinese national Guo Zhong Chen, of Belvedere Terrace, Mullingar, pleaded guilty to starting the fire and was due to be sentenced today. item.title: Ballymahon's Main Street remains closed
item.description: Main Street in Ballymahon remains closed this lunchtime. That's after a man in his 80s suffered serious injuries after being struck by car. The incident occurred at around 5.15pm on Monday evening and a pedestrian was rushed to Tullamore hospital. Advertisement The driver of the car, a man in his late teens, suffered no injuries. Gardai are continuing to appeal for witnesses to come forward.

item.title: Slovakian man appears in court over alleged Longford stabbing
item.description: A Slovakian man has appeared in court in relation to an alleged stabbing in Longford town last week. He was granted bail at Longford District Court today. 29-year-old Martin Grundza, with an address at 47 Lana Aoibheann, Longford, was charged with assault causing harm, under Section 3 of the Non-Fatal Offences Against the Person Act, to a man in his 30s last Wednesday at Chapel Lane in the town. item.title: Ricky O'Donnell
item.description: Ricky O'Donnell Late of Keshcarrigan and Belfast Ricky O'Donnell is sadly missed by his wide circle of friends in Leitrim, Belfast and Scotland. Reposing in Keshcarrigan on Wednesday 4th February from 6-9pm. Funeral mass on Thursday 5th February at 9am in Drumcong followed by cremation at 12 noon in Lakelands Crematorium Cavan. If you cannot attend the funeral or sympathise with the family, you can now leave your messages of condolences and memories on this page. We hold comments for moderation.

item.title: EU Commission tasked over South American stance
item.description: The European Commission have come under fire for their approach to South American beef. In December, it emerged that consignments of frozen Brazilian beef products contained a banned hormone. While at the start of January, the Department of Agriculture confirmed that 128kg of implicated beef was distributed to three food businesses in Ireland. item.title: Funeral of former Longford goalkeeper John Heneghan takes place
item.description: The funeral mass of John Heneghan has heard of his success on the Gaelic football field. The late Mr Heneghan enjoyed a sterling playing career with the county. He was goalkeeper on the county’s history-making 1966 National League and 1968 Leinster Senior Football Championship winning teams. Advertisement A Ballymahon clubman, he served as team mentor and goalkeeping coach in the 1980s and was named in the Longford 'Team of the Millennium' in 2000. item.title: Ballymahon's Main Street reopens
item.description: Main Street in Ballymahon has reopened. The road was closed overnight and into today after a man in his 80s suffered serious injuries after being hit by car at around 5.15pm on Monday evening. The pedestrian was rushed to Tullamore hospital. Advertisement The driver of the car, a man in his late teens, wasn't injured. Gardaí are continuing to appeal for witnesses to come forward.

item.title: Funeral of Derek Cobbe takes place
item.description: Tributes have been paid to well-known Longford newspaper editor Derek Cobbe, whose funeral took place today. Mr Cobbe of Gurteenorna, Longford and formerly of Rialto, Dublin, was a former editor of the Longford Leader and then proprietor and editor of the Longford News. He passed away on Friday last following a prolonged illness and was laid to rest this afternoon in Saint Paul’s Church Cemetery, Newtownforbes.
